headline: Quantum Dynamics, Hardware Limits, and Open Systems
summary: Today's crop explores non-equilibrium quantum physics, benchmarking limits, and state preparation. Papers span dissipative limits on ground states and noisy memory to concrete simulator readouts and hardware architectures across superconducting and trapped-ion systems.

themes.title: Dissipative Dynamics & Non-Equilibrium States
themes.body: Studies explore what states can be stabilized or probed under open, dissipative conditions, ranging from no-go theorems for local ground-state cooling to stochastic resetting steady states and uncoordinated classical memory protection.

themes.title: Quantum Hardware and Simulation Protocols
themes.body: New techniques optimize quantum processors and simulators, including smart snapshot readouts of hidden conserved quantities, evaluating multi-qubit entangling gates, and utilizing left-handed lines for vacuum photon generation.

connections.body: Both 2610.40652 and 2610.40638 extract complex dynamical properties (energy transport profiles and reset-time memory) from quantum devices using efficient single-basis measurement snapshots without postselection or full tomography.
Both 2610.40651 and 2610.40628 analyze fundamental spatial locality constraints in stabilizing target quantum and classical information under non-equilibrium dissipative updates.
